w: Then you will begin to say, ‘We ate and drank in your presence, and you taught in our streets.’
k: Then shall ye begin to say, We have eaten and drunk in thy presence, and thou hast taught in our streets.

w: I tell you, no, but unless you repent, you will all perish in the same way.
k: I tell you, Nay: but, except ye repent, ye shall all likewise perish.

w: He answered, ‘Lord, leave it alone this year also, until I dig around it, and fertilize it.
k: And he answering said unto him, Lord, let it alone this year also, till I shall dig about it, and dung it:

w: Ought not this woman, being a daughter of Abraham, whom Satan had bound eighteen long years, be freed from this bondage on the Sabbath day?”
k: And ought not this woman, being a daughter of Abraham, whom Satan hath bound, lo, these eighteen years, be loosed from this bond on the sabbath day?

w: They will come from the east, west, north, and south, and will sit down in God’s Kingdom.
k: And they shall come from the east, and from the west, and from the north, and from the south, and shall sit down in the kingdom of God.

w: Nevertheless I must go on my way today and tomorrow and the next day, for it can’t be that a prophet would perish outside of Jerusalem.’
k: Nevertheless I must walk to day, and to morrow, and the day following: for it cannot be that a prophet perish out of Jerusalem.

w: Behold, your house is left to you desolate. I tell you, you will not see me, until you say, ‘Blessed is he who comes in the name of the Lord!’”
k: Behold, your house is left unto you desolate: and verily I say unto you, Ye shall not see me, until the time come when ye shall say, Blessed is he that cometh in the name of the Lord.

w: There will be weeping and gnashing of teeth, when you see Abraham, Isaac, Jacob, and all the prophets, in God’s Kingdom, and yourselves being thrown outside.
k: There shall be weeping and gnashing of teeth, when ye shall see Abraham, and Isaac, and Jacob, and all the prophets, in the kingdom of God, and you yourselves thrust out.

w: It is like a grain of mustard seed, which a man took, and put in his own garden. It grew, and became a large tree, and the birds of the sky live in its branches.”
k: It is like a grain of mustard seed, which a man took, and cast into his garden; and it grew, and waxed a great tree; and the fowls of the air lodged in the branches of it.

w: If it bears fruit, fine; but if not, after that, you can cut it down.’”
k: And if it bear fruit, well: and if not, then after that thou shalt cut it down.

w: He said to the vine dresser, ‘Behold, these three years I have come looking for fruit on this fig tree, and found none. Cut it down. Why does it waste the soil?’
k: Then said he unto the dresser of his vineyard, Behold, these three years I come seeking fruit on this fig tree, and find none: cut it down; why cumbereth it the ground?

w: “To what shall I compare God’s Kingdom?
k: Whereunto shall I liken the kingdom of God?

w: “A certain man had a fig tree planted in his vineyard, and he came seeking fruit on it, and found none.
k: A certain man had a fig tree planted in his vineyard; and he came and sought fruit thereon, and found none.

w: It is like yeast, which a woman took and hid in three measures
of flour, until it was all leavened.”
k: It is like leaven, which a woman took and hid in three measures of meal, till the whole was leavened.

w: Or those eighteen, on whom the tower in Siloam fell, and killed them; do you think that they were worse offenders than all the men who dwell in Jerusalem?
k: Or those eighteen, upon whom the tower in Siloam fell, and slew them, think ye that they were sinners above all men that dwelt in Jerusalem?

w: I tell you, no, but, unless you repent, you will all perish in the same way.”
k: I tell you, Nay: but, except ye repent, ye shall all likewise perish.

w: “Strive to enter in by the narrow door, for many, I tell you, will seek to enter in, and will not be able.
k: Strive to enter in at the strait gate: for many, I say unto you, will seek to enter in, and shall not be able.

w: When once the master of the house has risen up, and has shut the door, and you begin to stand outside, and to knock at the door, saying, ‘Lord, Lord, open to us!’ then he will answer and tell you, ‘I don’t know you or where you come from.’
k: When once the master of the house is risen up, and hath shut to the door, and ye begin to stand without, and to knock at the door, saying, Lord, Lord, open unto us; and he shall answer and say unto you, I know you not whence ye are:

w: “Woman, you are freed from your infirmity.”
k: Woman, thou art loosed from thine infirmity.

w: Or perhaps, when he has laid a foundation, and is not able to finish, everyone who sees begins to mock him,
k: Lest haply, after he hath laid the foundation, and is not able to finish it, all that behold it begin to mock him,

w: “Which of you, if your son
or an ox fell into a well, wouldn’t immediately pull him out on a Sabbath day?”
k: Which of you shall have an ass or an ox fallen into a pit, and will not straightway pull him out on the sabbath day?

w: “Another said, ‘I have bought five yoke of oxen, and I must go try them out. Please have me excused.’
k: And another said, I have bought five yoke of oxen, and I go to prove them: I pray thee have me excused.

w: They all as one began to make excuses.
“The first said to him, ‘I have bought a field, and I must go and see it. Please have me excused.’
k: And they all with one consent began to make excuse. The first said unto him, I have bought a piece of ground, and I must needs go and see it: I pray thee have me excused.

w: “When you are invited by anyone to a marriage feast, don’t sit in the best seat, since perhaps someone more honorable than you might be invited by him,
k: When thou art bidden of any man to a wedding, sit not down in the highest room; lest a more honourable man than thou be bidden of him;

w: Or what king, as he goes to encounter another king in war, will not sit down first and consider whether he is able with ten thousand to meet him who comes against him with twenty thousand?
k: Or what king, going to make war against another king, sitteth not down first, and consulteth whether he be able with ten thousand to meet him that cometh against him with twenty thousand?

w: But when you make a feast, ask the poor, the maimed, the lame, or the blind;
k: But when thou makest a feast, call the poor, the maimed, the lame, the blind:

w: and he who invited both of you would come and tell you, ‘Make room for this person.’ Then you would begin, with shame, to take the lowest place.
k: And he that bade thee and him come and say to thee, Give this man place; and thou begin with shame to take the lowest room.

w: But when you are invited, go and sit in the lowest place, so that when he who invited you comes, he may tell you, ‘Friend, move up higher.’ Then you will be honored in the presence of all who sit at the table with you.
k: But when thou art bidden, go and sit down in the lowest room; that when he that bade thee cometh, he may say unto thee, Friend, go up higher: then shalt thou have worship in the presence of them that sit at meat with thee.

w: So therefore whoever of you who doesn’t renounce all that he has, he can’t be my disciple.
k: So likewise, whosoever he be of you that forsaketh not all that he hath, he cannot be my disciple.

w: Whoever doesn’t bear his own cross, and come after me, can’t be my disciple.
k: And whosoever doth not bear his cross, and come after me, cannot be my disciple.

w: “A certain man made a great supper, and he invited many people.
k: A certain man made a great supper, and bade many:

w: “That servant came, and told his lord these things. Then the master of the house, being angry, said to his servant, ‘Go out quickly into the streets and lanes of the city, and bring in the poor, maimed, blind, and lame.’
k: So that servant came, and shewed his lord these things. Then the master of the house being angry said to his servant, Go out quickly into the streets and lanes of the city, and bring in hither the poor, and the maimed, and the halt, and the blind.

w: “If anyone comes to me, and doesn’t disregard
his own father, mother, wife, children, brothers, and sisters, yes, and his own life also, he can’t be my disciple.
k: If any man come to me, and hate not his father, and mother, and wife, and children, and brethren, and sisters, yea, and his own life also, he cannot be my disciple.

w: “When you make a dinner or a supper, don’t call your friends, nor your brothers, nor your kinsmen, nor rich neighbors, or perhaps they might also return the favor, and pay you back.
k: When thou makest a dinner or a supper, call not thy friends, nor thy brethren, neither thy kinsmen, nor thy rich neighbours; lest they also bid thee again, and a recompence be made thee.

w: “Another said, ‘I have married a wife, and therefore I can’t come.’
k: And another said, I have married a wife, and therefore I cannot come.

w: Salt is good, but if the salt becomes flat and tasteless, with what do you season it?
k: Salt is good: but if the salt have lost his savour, wherewith shall it be seasoned?

w: and you will be blessed, because they don’t have the resources to repay you. For you will be repaid in the resurrection of the righteous.”
k: And thou shalt be blessed; for they cannot recompense thee: for thou shalt be recompensed at the resurrection of the just.

w: He sent out his servant at supper time to tell those who were invited, ‘Come, for everything is ready now.’
k: And sent his servant at supper time to say to them that were bidden, Come; for all things are now ready.

w: saying, ‘This man began to build, and wasn’t able to finish.’
k: Saying, This man began to build, and was not able to finish.

w: Or else, while the other is yet a great way off, he sends an envoy, and asks for conditions of peace.
k: Or else, while the other is yet a great way off, he sendeth an ambassage, and desireth conditions of peace.

w: It is fit neither for the soil nor for the manure pile. It is thrown out. He who has ears to hear, let him hear.”
k: It is neither fit for the land, nor yet for the dunghill; but men cast it out. He that hath ears to hear, let him hear.

w: For which of you, desiring to build a tower, doesn’t first sit down and count the cost, to see if he has enough to complete it?
k: For which of you, intending to build a tower, sitteth not down first, and counteth the cost, whether he have sufficient to finish it?

w: “Is it lawful to heal on the Sabbath?”
k: Is it lawful to heal on the sabbath day?

w: For everyone who exalts himself will be humbled, and whoever humbles himself will be exalted.”
k: For whosoever exalteth himself shall be abased; and he that humbleth himself shall be exalted.

w: For I tell you that none of those men who were invited will taste of my supper.’”
k: For I say unto you, That none of those men which were bidden shall taste of my supper.

w: “The lord said to the servant, ‘Go out into the highways and hedges, and compel them to come in, that my house may be filled.
k: And the lord said unto the servant, Go out into the highways and hedges, and compel them to come in, that my house may be filled.

w: “The servant said, ‘Lord, it is done as you commanded, and there is still room.’
k: And the servant said, Lord, it is done as thou hast commanded, and yet there is room.
And, behold, a woman in the city, which was a sinner, when she knew that Jesus sat at meat in the Pharisee’s house, brought an alabaster box of ointment,
And when they came to Jesus, they besought him instantly, saying, That he was worthy for whom he should do this:

w: When they couldn’t pay, he forgave them both. Which of them therefore will love him most?”
k: And when they had nothing to pay, he frankly forgave them both. Tell me therefore, which of them will love him most?
Now when he had ended all his sayings in the audience of the people, he entered into Capernaum.

w: They are like children who sit in the marketplace, and call to one another, saying, ‘We piped to you, and you didn’t dance. We mourned, and you didn’t weep.’
k: They are like unto children sitting in the marketplace, and calling one to another, and saying, We have piped unto you, and ye have not danced; we have mourned to you, and ye have not wept.
And a certain centurion’s servant, who was dear unto him, was sick, and ready to die.
And stood at his feet behind him weeping, and began to wash his feet with tears, and did wipe them with the hairs of her head, and kissed his feet, and anointed them with the ointment.

w: “Do you see this woman? I entered into your house, and you gave me no water for my feet, but she has wet my feet with her tears, and wiped them with the hair of her head.
k: Seest thou this woman? I entered into thine house, thou gavest me no water for my feet: but she hath washed my feet with tears, and wiped them with the hairs of her head.

w: “Young man, I tell you, arise!”
k: Young man, I say unto thee, Arise.

w: “A certain lender had two debtors. The one owed five hundred denarii, and the other fifty.
k: There was a certain creditor which had two debtors: the one owed five hundred pence, and the other fifty.

w: “You have judged correctly.”
k: Thou hast rightly judged.

w: But what did you go out to see? A prophet? Yes, I tell you, and much more than a prophet.
k: But what went ye out for to see? A prophet? Yea, I say unto you, and much more than a prophet.

w: “What did you go out into the wilderness to see? A reed shaken by the wind?
k: And when the messengers of John were departed, he began to speak unto the people concerning John, What went ye out into the wilderness for to see? A reed shaken with the wind?
Wherefore neither thought I myself worthy to come unto thee: but say in a word, and my servant shall be healed.

w: The Son of Man has come eating and drinking, and you say, ‘Behold, a gluttonous man, and a drunkard; a friend of tax collectors and sinners!’
k: The Son of man is come eating and drinking; and ye say, Behold a gluttonous man, and a winebibber, a friend of publicans and sinners!
And when he heard of Jesus, he sent unto him the elders of the Jews, beseeching him that he would come and heal his servant.

w: For John the Baptizer came neither eating bread nor drinking wine, and you say, ‘He has a demon.’
k: For John the Baptist came neither eating bread nor drinking wine; and ye say, He hath a devil.

w: Wisdom is justified by all her children.”
k: But wisdom is justified of all her children.

w: “Don’t cry.”
k: Weep not.

w: Blessed is he who finds no occasion for stumbling in me.”
k: And blessed is he, whosoever shall not be offended in me.

w: You didn’t anoint my head with oil, but she has anointed my feet with ointment.
k: My head with oil thou didst not anoint: but this woman hath anointed my feet with ointment.

w: “Simon, I have something to tell you.”
k: And Jesus answering said unto him, Simon, I have somewhat to say unto thee.

w: Therefore I tell you, her sins, which are many, are forgiven, for she loved much. But to whom little is forgiven, the same loves little.”
k: Wherefore I say unto thee, Her sins, which are many, are forgiven; for she loved much: but to whom little is forgiven, the same loveth little.

Now when the Pharisee which had bidden him saw it, he spake within himself, saying, This man, if he were a prophet, would have known who and what manner of woman this is that toucheth him: for she is a sinner.
And one of the Pharisees desired him that he would eat with him. And he went into the Pharisee’s house, and sat down to meat.

w: “Go and tell John the things which you have seen and heard: that the blind receive their sight, the lame walk, the lepers are cleansed, the deaf hear, the dead are raised up, and the poor have good news preached to them.
k: Go your way, and tell John what things ye have seen and heard; how that the blind see, the lame walk, the lepers are cleansed, the deaf hear, the dead are raised, to the poor the gospel is preached.

w: But what did you go out to see? A man clothed in soft clothing? Behold, those who are gorgeously dressed, and live delicately, are in kings’ courts.
k: But what went ye out for to see? A man clothed in soft raiment? Behold, they which are gorgeously apparelled, and live delicately, are in kings courts.

w: “I tell you, I have not found such great faith, no, not in Israel.”
k: When Jesus heard these things, he marvelled at him, and turned him about, and said unto the people that followed him, I say unto you, I have not found so great faith, no, not in Israel.
For he loveth our nation, and he hath built us a synagogue.
For I also am a man set under authority, having under me soldiers, and I say unto one, Go, and he goeth; and to another, Come, and he cometh; and to my servant, Do this, and he doeth it.

w: “To what then will I liken the people of this generation? What are they like?
k: Whereunto then shall I liken the men of this generation? and to what are they like?

w: “For I tell you, among those who are born of women there is not a greater prophet than John the Baptizer, yet he who is least in God’s Kingdom is greater than he.”
k: For I say unto you, Among those that are born of women there is not a greater prophet than John the Baptist: but he that is least in the kingdom of God is greater than he.

Then Jesus went with them. And when he was now not far from the house, the centurion sent friends to him, saying unto him, Lord, trouble not thyself: for I am not worthy that thou shouldest enter under my roof:

w: You gave me no kiss, but she, since the time I came in, has not ceased to kiss my feet.
k: Thou gavest me no kiss: but this woman since the time I came in hath not ceased to kiss my feet.

w: “Your faith has saved you. Go in peace.”
k: Thy faith hath saved thee; go in peace.

w: “Your sins are forgiven.”
k: Thy sins are forgiven.

w: This is he of whom it is written,
‘Behold, I send my messenger before your face,
who will prepare your way before you.’
k: This is he, of whom it is written, Behold, I send my messenger before thy face, which shall prepare thy way before thee.

w: “When you pray, say,
‘Our Father in heaven,
may your name be kept holy.
May your Kingdom come.
May your will be done on earth, as it is in heaven.
k: When ye pray, say, Our Father which art in heaven, Hallowed be thy name. Thy kingdom come. Thy will be done, as in heaven, so in earth.

w: But if I by God’s finger cast out demons, then God’s Kingdom has come to you.
k: But if I with the finger of God cast out devils, no doubt the kingdom of God is come upon you.

w: “Woe to you lawyers also! For you load men with burdens that are difficult to carry, and you yourselves won’t even lift one finger to help carry those burdens.
k: Woe unto you also, ye lawyers! for ye lade men with burdens grievous to be borne, and ye yourselves touch not the burdens with one of your fingers.

w: But give for gifts to the needy those things which are within, and behold, all things will be clean to you.
k: But rather give alms of such things as ye have; and, behold, all things are clean unto you.

w: “This is an evil generation. It seeks after a sign. No sign will be given to it but the sign of Jonah, the prophet.
k: This is an evil generation: they seek a sign; and there shall no sign be given it, but the sign of Jonas the prophet.

w: Therefore also the wisdom of God said, ‘I will send to them prophets and apostles; and some of them they will kill and persecute,
k: Therefore also said the wisdom of God, I will send them prophets and apostles, and some of them they shall slay and persecute:

w: “On the contrary, blessed are those who hear the word of God, and keep it.”
k: Yea rather, blessed are they that hear the word of God, and keep it.

w: Give us day by day our daily bread.
k: Give us day by day our daily bread.

w: If Satan also is divided against himself, how will his kingdom stand? For you say that I cast out demons by Beelzebul.
k: If Satan also be divided against himself, how shall his kingdom stand? because ye say that I cast out devils through Beelzebub.

w: I tell you, although he will not rise and give it to him because he is his friend, yet because of his persistence, he will get up and give him as many as he needs.
k: I say unto you, Though he will not rise and give him, because he is his friend, yet because of his importunity he will rise and give him as many as he needeth.

w: Then he goes, and takes seven other spirits more evil than himself, and they enter in and dwell there. The last state of that man becomes worse than the first.”
k: Then goeth he, and taketh to him seven other spirits more wicked than himself; and they enter in, and dwell there: and the last state of that man is worse than the first.

w: Woe to you, scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites! For you are like hidden graves, and the men who walk over them don’t know it.”
k: Woe unto you, scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites! for ye are as graves which appear not, and the men that walk over them are not aware of them.

w: Therefore see whether the light that is in you isn’t darkness.
k: Take heed therefore that the light which is in thee be not darkness.

w: “I tell you, keep asking, and it will be given you. Keep seeking, and you will find. Keep knocking, and it will be opened to you.
k: And I say unto you, Ask, and it shall be given you; seek, and ye shall find; knock, and it shall be opened unto you.

w: “No one, when he has lit a lamp, puts it in a cellar or under a basket, but on a stand, that those who come in may see the light.
k: No man, when he hath lighted a candle, putteth it in a secret place, neither under a bushel, but on a candlestick, that they which come in may see the light.

w: Woe to you! For you build the tombs of the prophets, and your fathers killed them.
k: Woe unto you! for ye build the sepulchres of the prophets, and your fathers killed them.

w: “Every kingdom divided against itself is brought to desolation. A house divided against itself falls.
k: Every kingdom divided against itself is brought to desolation; and a house divided against a house falleth.

w: The lamp of the body is the eye. Therefore when your eye is good, your whole body is also full of light; but when it is evil, your body also is full of darkness.
k: The light of the body is the eye: therefore when thine eye is single, thy whole body also is full of light; but when thine eye is evil, thy body also is full of darkness.

w: that the blood of all the prophets, which was shed from the foundation of the world, may be required of this generation;
k: That the blood of all the prophets, which was shed from the foundation of the world, may be required of this generation;

w: For even as Jonah became a sign to the Ninevites, so will also the Son of Man be to this generation.
k: For as Jonas was a sign unto the Ninevites, so shall also the Son of man be to this generation.

w: The unclean spirit, when he has gone out of the man, passes through dry places, seeking rest, and finding none, he says, ‘I will turn back to my house from which I came out.’
k: When the unclean spirit is gone out of a man, he walketh through dry places, seeking rest; and finding none, he saith, I will return unto my house whence I came out.

w: Or if he asks for an egg, he won’t give him a scorpion, will he?
k: Or if he shall ask an egg, will he offer him a scorpion?

w: Woe to you lawyers! For you took away the key of knowledge. You didn’t enter in yourselves, and those who were entering in, you hindered.”
k: Woe unto you, lawyers! for ye have taken away the key of knowledge: ye entered not in yourselves, and them that were entering in ye hindered.

w: You foolish ones, didn’t he who made the outside make the inside also?
k: Ye fools, did not he that made that which is without make that which is within also?

w: Woe to you Pharisees! For you love the best seats in the synagogues, and the greetings in the marketplaces.
k: Woe unto you, Pharisees! for ye love the uppermost seats in the synagogues, and greetings in the markets.

w: But woe to you Pharisees! For you tithe mint and rue and every herb, but you bypass justice and God’s love. You ought to have done these, and not to have left the other undone.
k: But woe unto you, Pharisees! for ye tithe mint and rue and all manner of herbs, and pass over judgment and the love of God: these ought ye to have done, and not to leave the other undone.

w: “Which of you, if you go to a friend at midnight, and tell him, ‘Friend, lend me three loaves of bread,
k: Which of you shall have a friend, and shall go unto him at midnight, and say unto him, Friend, lend me three loaves;

w: But if I cast out demons by Beelzebul, by whom do your children cast them out? Therefore will they be your judges.
k: And if I by Beelzebub cast out devils, by whom do your sons cast them out? therefore shall they be your judges.

w: The Queen of the South will rise up in the judgment with the men of this generation, and will condemn them: for she came from the ends of the earth to hear the wisdom of Solomon; and behold, one greater than Solomon is here.
k: The queen of the south shall rise up in the judgment with the men of this generation, and condemn them: for she came from the utmost parts of the earth to hear the wisdom of Solomon; and, behold, a greater than Solomon is here.

w: for a friend of mine has come to me from a journey, and I have nothing to set before him,’
k: For a friend of mine in his journey is come to me, and I have nothing to set before him?

w: If you then, being evil, know how to give good gifts to your children, how much more will your heavenly Father give the Holy Spirit to those who ask him?”
k: If ye then, being evil, know how to give good gifts unto your children: how much more shall your heavenly Father give the Holy Spirit to them that ask him?

w: “Which of you fathers, if your son asks for bread, will give him a stone? Or if he asks for a fish, he won’t give him a snake instead of a fish, will he?
k: If a son shall ask bread of any of you that is a father, will he give him a stone? or if he ask a fish, will he for a fish give him a serpent?

w: For everyone who asks receives. He who seeks finds. To him who knocks it will be opened.
k: For every one that asketh receiveth; and he that seeketh findeth; and to him that knocketh it shall be opened.

w: The men of Nineveh will stand up in the judgment with this generation, and will condemn it: for they repented at the preaching of Jonah, and behold, one greater than Jonah is here.
k: The men of Nineve shall rise up in the judgment with this generation, and shall condemn it: for they repented at the preaching of Jonas; and, behold, a greater than Jonas is here.

w: “Now you Pharisees cleanse the outside of the cup and of the platter, but your inward part is full of extortion and wickedness.
k: Now do ye Pharisees make clean the outside of the cup and the platter; but your inward part is full of ravening and wickedness.

w: So you testify and consent to the works of your fathers. For they killed them, and you build their tombs.
k: Truly ye bear witness that ye allow the deeds of your fathers: for they indeed killed them, and ye build their sepulchres.

w: But when someone stronger attacks him and overcomes him, he takes from him his whole armor in which he trusted, and divides his plunder.
k: But when a stronger than he shall come upon him, and overcome him, he taketh from him all his armour wherein he trusted, and divideth his spoils.

w: and he from within will answer and say, ‘Don’t bother me. The door is now shut, and my children are with me in bed. I can’t get up and give it to you’?
k: And he from within shall answer and say, Trouble me not: the door is now shut, and my children are with me in bed; I cannot rise and give thee.

w: “When the strong man, fully armed, guards his own dwelling, his goods are safe.
k: When a strong man armed keepeth his palace, his goods are in peace:

w: “He that is not with me is against me. He who doesn’t gather with me scatters.
k: He that is not with me is against me: and he that gathereth not with me scattereth.

w: If therefore your whole body is full of light, having no part dark, it will be wholly full of light, as when the lamp with its bright shining gives you light.”
k: If thy whole body therefore be full of light, having no part dark, the whole shall be full of light, as when the bright shining of a candle doth give thee light.

w: When he returns, he finds it swept and put in order.
k: And when he cometh, he findeth it swept and garnished.

w: Forgive us our sins,
for we ourselves also forgive everyone who is indebted to us.
Bring us not into temptation,
but deliver us from the evil one.’”
k: And forgive us our sins; for we also forgive every one that is indebted to us. And lead us not into temptation; but deliver us from evil.

w: from the blood of Abel to the blood of Zachariah, who perished between the altar and the sanctuary.’ Yes, I tell you, it will be required of this generation.
k: From the blood of Abel unto the blood of Zacharias, which perished between the altar and the temple: verily I say unto you, It shall be required of this generation.

w: Rejoice in that day, and leap for joy, for behold, your reward is great in heaven, for their fathers did the same thing to the prophets.
k: Rejoice ye in that day, and leap for joy: for, behold, your reward is great in heaven: for in the like manner did their fathers unto the prophets.

w: Give to everyone who asks you, and don’t ask him who takes away your goods to give them back again.
k: Give to every man that asketh of thee; and of him that taketh away thy goods ask them not again.

w: “But I tell you who hear: love your enemies, do good to those who hate you,
k: But I say unto you which hear, Love your enemies, do good to them which hate you,

w: “But woe to you who are rich!
For you have received your consolation.
k: But woe unto you that are rich! for ye have received your consolation.

w: Woe,
when
men speak well of you,
for their fathers did the same thing to the false prophets.
k: Woe unto you, when all men shall speak well of you! for so did their fathers to the false prophets.

w: Blessed are you who hunger now,
for you will be filled.
Blessed are you who weep now,
for you will laugh.
k: Blessed are ye that hunger now: for ye shall be filled. Blessed are ye that weep now: for ye shall laugh.

w: Or how can you tell your brother, ‘Brother, let me remove the speck of chaff that is in your eye,’ when you yourself don’t see the beam that is in your own eye? You hypocrite! First remove the beam from your own eye, and then you can see clearly to remove the speck of chaff that is in your brother’s eye.
k: Either how canst thou say to thy brother, Brother, let me pull out the mote that is in thine eye, when thou thyself beholdest not the beam that is in thine own eye? Thou hypocrite, cast out first the beam out of thine own eye, and then shalt thou see clearly to pull out the mote that is in thy brother’s eye.

w: To him who strikes you on the cheek, offer also the other; and from him who takes away your cloak, don’t withhold your coat also.
k: And unto him that smiteth thee on the one cheek offer also the other; and him that taketh away thy cloke forbid not to take thy coat also.

w: If you love those who love you, what credit is that to you? For even sinners love those who love them.
k: For if ye love them which love you, what thank have ye? for sinners also love those that love them.

w: A disciple is not above his teacher, but everyone when he is fully trained will be like his teacher.
k: The disciple is not above his master: but every one that is perfect shall be as his master.

w: But he who hears, and doesn’t do, is like a man who built a house on the earth without a foundation, against which the stream broke, and immediately it fell, and the ruin of that house was great.”
k: But he that heareth, and doeth not, is like a man that without a foundation built an house upon the earth; against which the stream did beat vehemently, and immediately it fell; and the ruin of that house was great.

w: Woe to you, you who are full now,
for you will be hungry.
Woe to you who laugh now,
for you will mourn and weep.
k: Woe unto you that are full! for ye shall hunger. Woe unto you that laugh now! for ye shall mourn and weep.

w: Blessed are you when men shall hate you, and when they shall exclude and mock you, and throw out your name as evil, for the Son of Man’s sake.
k: Blessed are ye, when men shall hate you, and when they shall separate you from their company, and shall reproach you, and cast out your name as evil, for the Son of man’s sake.

w: “Blessed are you who are poor,
God’s Kingdom is yours.
k: Blessed be ye poor: for yours is the kingdom of God.

w: “Haven’t you read what David did when he was hungry, he, and those who were with him;
k: Have ye not read so much as this, what David did, when himself was an hungred, and they which were with him;

w: “I will ask you something: Is it lawful on the Sabbath to do good, or to do harm? To save a life, or to kill?”
k: I will ask you one thing; Is it lawful on the sabbath days to do good, or to do evil? to save life, or to destroy it?

w: Everyone who comes to me, and hears my words, and does them, I will show you who he is like.
k: Whosoever cometh to me, and heareth my sayings, and doeth them, I will shew you to whom he is like:

w: The good man out of the good treasure of his heart brings out that which is good, and the evil man out of the evil treasure of his heart brings out that which is evil, for out of the abundance of the heart, his mouth speaks.
k: A good man out of the good treasure of his heart bringeth forth that which is good; and an evil man out of the evil treasure of his heart bringeth forth that which is evil: for of the abundance of the heart his mouth speaketh.

w: “Why do you call me, ‘Lord, Lord,’ and don’t do the things which I say?
k: And why call ye me, Lord, Lord, and do not the things which I say?

w: Why do you see the speck of chaff that is in your brother’s eye, but don’t consider the beam that is in your own eye?
k: And why beholdest thou the mote that is in thy brother’s eye, but perceivest not the beam that is in thine own eye?

w: Don’t judge,
and you won’t be judged.
Don’t condemn,
and you won’t be condemned.
Set free,
and you will be set free.
k: Judge not, and ye shall not be judged: condemn not, and ye shall not be condemned: forgive, and ye shall be forgiven:

w: “Rise up, and stand in the middle.”
k: Rise up, and stand forth in the midst.

w: But love your enemies, and do good, and lend, expecting nothing back; and your reward will be great, and you will be children of the Most High; for he is kind toward the unthankful and evil.
k: But love ye your enemies, and do good, and lend, hoping for nothing again; and your reward shall be great, and ye shall be the children of the Highest: for he is kind unto the unthankful and to the evil.

w: If you lend to those from whom you hope to receive, what credit is that to you? Even sinners lend to sinners, to receive back as much.
k: And if ye lend to them of whom ye hope to receive, what thank have ye? for sinners also lend to sinners, to receive as much again.

w: “Stretch out your hand.”
k: Stretch forth thy hand.

w: how he entered into God’s house, and took and ate the show bread, and gave also to those who were with him, which is not lawful to eat except for the priests alone?”
k: How he went into the house of God, and did take and eat the shewbread, and gave also to them that were with him; which it is not lawful to eat but for the priests alone?

w: “As you would like people to do to you, do exactly so to them.
k: And as ye would that men should do to you, do ye also to them likewise.

w: “The Son of Man is lord of the Sabbath.”
k: That the Son of man is Lord also of the sabbath.

w: “Therefore be merciful,
even as your Father is also merciful.
k: Be ye therefore merciful, as your Father also is merciful.

w: bless those who curse you, and pray for those who mistreat you.
k: Bless them that curse you, and pray for them which despitefully use you.

w: “Give, and it will be given to you: good measure, pressed down, shaken together, and running over, will be given to you.
For with the same measure you measure it will be measured back to you.”
k: Give, and it shall be given unto you; good measure, pressed down, and shaken together, and running over, shall men give into your bosom. For with the same measure that ye mete withal it shall be measured to you again.

w: For there is no good tree that produces rotten fruit; nor again a rotten tree that produces good fruit.
k: For a good tree bringeth not forth corrupt fruit; neither doth a corrupt tree bring forth good fruit.

w: “Can the blind guide the blind? Won’t they both fall into a pit?
k: Can the blind lead the blind? shall they not both fall into the ditch?

w: For each tree is known by its own fruit. For people don’t gather figs from thorns, nor do they gather grapes from a bramble bush.
k: For every tree is known by his own fruit. For of thorns men do not gather figs, nor of a bramble bush gather they grapes.

w: If you do good to those who do good to you, what credit is that to you? For even sinners do the same.
k: And if ye do good to them which do good to you, what thank have ye? for sinners also do even the same.

w: He is like a man building a house, who dug and went deep, and laid a foundation on the rock. When a flood arose, the stream broke against that house, and could not shake it, because it was founded on the rock.
k: He is like a man which built an house, and digged deep, and laid the foundation on a rock: and when the flood arose, the stream beat vehemently upon that house, and could not shake it: for it was founded upon a rock.

w: Those along the road are those who hear, then the devil comes, and takes away the word from their heart, that they may not believe and be saved.
k: Those by the way side are they that hear; then cometh the devil, and taketh away the word out of their hearts, lest they should believe and be saved.

w: Those in the good ground, these are those who with an honest and good heart, having heard the word, hold it tightly, and produce fruit with perseverance.
k: But that on the good ground are they, which in an honest and good heart, having heard the word, keep it, and bring forth fruit with patience.

w: Other fell amid the thorns, and the thorns grew with it, and choked it.
k: And some fell among thorns; and the thorns sprang up with it, and choked it.

w: “My mother and my brothers are these who hear the word of God, and do it.”
k: My mother and my brethren are these which hear the word of God, and do it.

w: “Return to your house, and declare what great things God has done for you.”
k: Return to thine own house, and shew how great things God hath done unto thee.

w: “Who touched me?”
‘Who touched me?’
k: Who touched me?Who touched me?

w: “Someone did touch me, for I perceived that power has gone out of me.”
k: Somebody hath touched me: for I perceive that virtue is gone out of me.

w: “Child, arise!”
k: Maid, arise.

w: Other seed fell on the rock, and as soon as it grew, it withered away, because it had no moisture.
k: And some fell upon a rock; and as soon as it was sprung up, it withered away, because it lacked moisture.

w: “To you it is given to know the mysteries of God’s Kingdom, but to the rest in parables; that ‘seeing they may not see, and hearing they may not understand.’
k: Unto you it is given to know the mysteries of the kingdom of God: but to others in parables; that seeing they might not see, and hearing they might not understand.

w: Those on the rock are they who, when they hear, receive the word with joy; but these have no root, who believe for a while, then fall away in time of temptation.
k: They on the rock are they, which, when they hear, receive the word with joy; and these have no root, which for a while believe, and in time of temptation fall away.

w: “Let’s go over to the other side of the lake.”
k: Let us go over unto the other side of the lake.

w: Other fell into the good ground, and grew, and produced one hundred times as much fruit.”
“He who has ears to hear, let him hear!”
k: And other fell on good ground, and sprang up, and bare fruit an hundredfold.He that hath ears to hear, let him hear.

w: Now the parable is this: The seed is the word of God.
k: Now the parable is this: The seed is the word of God.

w: That which fell among the thorns, these are those who have heard, and as they go on their way they are choked with cares, riches, and pleasures of life, and bring no fruit to maturity.
k: And that which fell among thorns are they, which, when they have heard, go forth, and are choked with cares and riches and pleasures of this life, and bring no fruit to perfection.

w: “No one, when he has lit a lamp, covers it with a container, or puts it under a bed; but puts it on a stand, that those who enter in may see the light.
k: No man, when he hath lighted a candle, covereth it with a vessel, or putteth it under a bed; but setteth it on a candlestick, that they which enter in may see the light.

w: “Where is your faith?”
k: Where is your faith?

w: “Don’t be afraid. Only believe, and she will be healed.”
k: Fear not: believe only, and she shall be made whole.

w: For nothing is hidden, that will not be revealed; nor anything secret, that will not be known and come to light.
k: For nothing is secret, that shall not be made manifest; neither any thing hid, that shall not be known and come abroad.

w: “What is your name?”
k: What is thy name?

w: “Daughter, cheer up. Your faith has made you well. Go in peace.”
k: Daughter, be of good comfort: thy faith hath made thee whole; go in peace.

w: “The farmer went out to sow his seed. As he sowed, some fell along the road, and it was trampled under foot, and the birds of the sky devoured it.
k: A sower went out to sow his seed: and as he sowed, some fell by the way side; and it was trodden down, and the fowls of the air devoured it.

w: Be careful therefore how you hear. For whoever has, to him will be given; and whoever doesn’t have, from him will be taken away even that which he thinks he has.”
k: Take heed therefore how ye hear: for whosoever hath, to him shall be given; and whosoever hath not, from him shall be taken even that which he seemeth to have.

w: “Don’t weep. She isn’t dead, but sleeping.”
k: Weep not; she is not dead, but sleepeth.

w: “Father, if you are willing, remove this cup from me. Nevertheless, not my will, but yours, be done.”
k: Father, if thou be willing, remove this cup from me: nevertheless not my will, but thine, be done.

w: “Take this, and share it among yourselves,
k: Take this, and divide it among yourselves:

w: For I tell you that this which is written must still be fulfilled in me: ‘He was counted with transgressors.’
For that which concerns me has an end.”
k: For I say unto you, that this that is written must yet be accomplished in me, And he was reckoned among the transgressors: for the things concerning me have an end.

w: “Judas, do you betray the Son of Man with a kiss?”
k: Judas, betrayest thou the Son of man with a kiss?

w: “Have you come out as against a robber, with swords and clubs?
k: Be ye come out, as against a thief, with swords and staves?

w: “This cup is the new covenant in my blood, which is poured out for you.
k: This cup is the new testament in my blood, which is shed for you.

w: From now on, the Son of Man will be seated at the right hand of the power of God.”
k: Hereafter shall the Son of man sit on the right hand of the power of God.

w: for I tell you, I will no longer by any means eat of it until it is fulfilled in God’s Kingdom.”
k: For I say unto you, I will not any more eat thereof, until it be fulfilled in the kingdom of God.

w: But behold, the hand of him who betrays me is with me on the table.
k: But, behold, the hand of him that betrayeth me is with me on the table.

w: “Let me at least do this”
k: Suffer ye thus far.

w: “Go and prepare the Passover for us, that we may eat.”
k: Go and prepare us the passover, that we may eat.

w: Tell the master of the house, ‘The Teacher says to you, “Where is the guest room, where I may eat the Passover with my disciples?”’
k: And ye shall say unto the goodman of the house, The Master saith unto thee, Where is the guestchamber, where I shall eat the passover with my disciples?

w: For who is greater, one who sits at the table, or one who serves? Isn’t it he who sits at the table? But I am among you as one who serves.
k: For whether is greater, he that sitteth at meat, or he that serveth? is not he that sitteth at meat? but I am among you as he that serveth.

w: When I was with you in the temple daily, you didn’t stretch out your hands against me. But this is your hour, and the power of darkness.”
k: When I was daily with you in the temple, ye stretched forth no hands against me: but this is your hour, and the power of darkness.

w: that you may eat and drink at my table in my Kingdom. You will sit on thrones, judging the twelve tribes of Israel.”
k: That ye may eat and drink at my table in my kingdom, and sit on thrones judging the twelve tribes of Israel.

w: but I prayed for you, that your faith wouldn’t fail. You, when once you have turned again, establish your brothers.”
k: But I have prayed for thee, that thy faith fail not: and when thou art converted, strengthen thy brethren.

w: “The kings of the nations lord it over them, and those who have authority over them are called ‘benefactors.’
k: The kings of the Gentiles exercise lordship over them; and they that exercise authority upon them are called benefactors.

w: “This is my body which is given for you. Do this in memory of me.”
k: This is my body which is given for you: this do in remembrance of me.

w: “Pray that you don’t enter into temptation.”
k: Pray that ye enter not into temptation.

w: The Son of Man indeed goes, as it has been determined, but woe to that man through whom he is betrayed!”
k: And truly the Son of man goeth, as it was determined: but woe unto that man by whom he is betrayed!

w: “Before the rooster crows you will deny me three times.”
I confer on you a kingdom, even as my Father conferred on me,
k: And I appoint unto you a kingdom, as my Father hath appointed unto me;

w: “Behold, when you have entered into the city, a man carrying a pitcher of water will meet you. Follow him into the house which he enters.
k: Behold, when ye are entered into the city, there shall a man meet you, bearing a pitcher of water; follow him into the house where he entereth in.

w: “Why do you sleep? Rise and pray that you may not enter into temptation.”
k: Why sleep ye? rise and pray, lest ye enter into temptation.

w: “Simon, Simon, behold, Satan asked to have all of you, that he might sift you as wheat,
k: Simon, Simon, behold, Satan hath desired to have you, that he may sift you as wheat:

w: But you are those who have continued with me in my trials.
k: Ye are they which have continued with me in my temptations.

w: He will show you a large, furnished upper room. Make preparations there.”
k: And he shall shew you a large upper room furnished: there make ready.

w: “You say it, because I am.”
k: Ye say that I am.

w: “I tell you, Peter, the rooster will by no means crow today until you deny that you know me three times.”
k: I tell thee, Peter, the cock shall not crow this day, before that thou shalt thrice deny that thou knowest me.

w: But not so with you. But one who is the greater among you, let him become as the younger, and one who is governing, as one who serves.
k: But ye shall not be so: but he that is greatest among you, let him be as the younger; and he that is chief, as he that doth serve.

w: “If I tell you, you won’t believe,
k: If I tell you, ye will not believe:

w: “But now, whoever has a purse, let him take it, and likewise a wallet. Whoever has none, let him sell his cloak, and buy a sword.
k: But now, he that hath a purse, let him take it, and likewise his scrip: and he that hath no sword, let him sell his garment, and buy one.

w: “When I sent you out without purse, and wallet, and shoes, did you lack anything?”
k: When I sent you without purse, and scrip, and shoes, lacked ye any thing?

w: “I have earnestly desired to eat this Passover with you before I suffer,
k: With desire I have desired to eat this passover with you before I suffer:

w: and if I ask, you will in no way answer me or let me go.
k: And if I also ask you, ye will not answer me, nor let me go.

w: for I tell you, I will not drink at all again from the fruit of the vine, until God’s Kingdom comes.”
k: For I say unto you, I will not drink of the fruit of the vine, until the kingdom of God shall come.

w: “That is enough.”
k: It is enough.

w: Does he thank that servant because he did the things that were commanded? I think not.
k: Doth he thank that servant because he did the things that were commanded him? I trow not.

w: They ate, they drank, they married, they were given in marriage, until the day that Noah entered into the ship, and the flood came, and destroyed them all.
k: They did eat, they drank, they married wives, they were given in marriage, until the day that Noe entered into the ark, and the flood came, and destroyed them all.
Two men shall be in the field; the one shall be taken, and the other left.

w: But first, he must suffer many things and be rejected by this generation.
k: But first must he suffer many things, and be rejected of this generation.

w: It would be better for him if a millstone were hung around his neck, and he were thrown into the sea, rather than that he should cause one of these little ones to stumble.
k: It were better for him that a millstone were hanged about his neck, and he cast into the sea, than that he should offend one of these little ones.

w: But who is there among you, having a servant plowing or keeping sheep, that will say, when he comes in from the field, ‘Come immediately and sit down at the table,’
k: But which of you, having a servant plowing or feeding cattle, will say unto him by and by, when he is come from the field, Go and sit down to meat?

w: Were there none found who returned to give glory to God, except this stranger?”
k: There are not found that returned to give glory to God, save this stranger.

w: “If you had faith like a grain of mustard seed, you would tell this sycamore tree, ‘Be uprooted, and be planted in the sea,’ and it would obey you.
k: If ye had faith as a grain of mustard seed, ye might say unto this sycamine tree, Be thou plucked up by the root, and be thou planted in the sea; and it should obey you.

w: As it was in the days of Noah, even so will it be also in the days of the Son of Man.
k: And as it was in the days of Noe, so shall it be also in the days of the Son of man.

w: “God’s Kingdom doesn’t come with observation;
k: The kingdom of God cometh not with observation:

w: Even so you also, when you have done all the things that are commanded you, say, ‘We are unworthy servants. We have done our duty.’”
k: So likewise ye, when ye shall have done all those things which are commanded you, say, We are unprofitable servants: we have done that which was our duty to do.

w: If he sins against you seven times in the day, and seven times returns, saying, ‘I repent,’ you shall forgive him.”
k: And if he trespass against thee seven times in a day, and seven times in a day turn again to thee, saying, I repent; thou shalt forgive him.

w: “Get up, and go your way. Your faith has healed you.”
k: Arise, go thy way: thy faith hath made thee whole.

w: Whoever seeks to save his life loses it, but whoever loses his life preserves it.
k: Whosoever shall seek to save his life shall lose it; and whosoever shall lose his life shall preserve it.

w: I tell you, in that night there will be two people in one bed. The one will be taken, and the other will be left.
k: I tell you, in that night there shall be two men in one bed; the one shall be taken, and the other shall be left.

w: It will be the same way in the day that the Son of Man is revealed.
k: Even thus shall it be in the day when the Son of man is revealed.

w: but in the day that Lot went out from Sodom, it rained fire and sulfur from the sky, and destroyed them all.
k: But the same day that Lot went out of Sodom it rained fire and brimstone from heaven, and destroyed them all.

w: Be careful. If your brother sins against you, rebuke him. If he repents, forgive him.
k: Take heed to yourselves: If thy brother trespass against thee, rebuke him; and if he repent, forgive him.

w: Remember Lot’s wife!
k: Remember Lot’s wife.

w: They will tell you, ‘Look, here!’ or ‘Look, there!’ Don’t go away, nor follow after them,
k: And they shall say to you, See here; or, see there: go not after them, nor follow them.

w: neither will they say, ‘Look, here!’ or, ‘Look, there!’ for behold, God’s Kingdom is within you.”
k: Neither shall they say, Lo here! or, lo there! for, behold, the kingdom of God is within you.

w: “The days will come, when you will desire to see one of the days of the Son of Man, and you will not see it.
k: The days will come, when ye shall desire to see one of the days of the Son of man, and ye shall not see

w: for as the lightning, when it flashes out of the one part under the sky, shines to the other part under the sky; so will the Son of Man be in his day.
k: For as the lightning, that lighteneth out of the one part under heaven, shineth unto the other part under heaven; so shall also the Son of man be in his day.

w: There will be two grinding grain together. One will be taken, and the other will be left.”
k: Two women shall be grinding together; the one shall be taken, and the other left.

w: “Weren’t the ten cleansed? But where are the nine?
k: Were there not ten cleansed? but where are the nine?

w: “Go and show yourselves to the priests.”
k: Go shew yourselves unto the priests. And it came to pass, that, as they went, they were cleansed.

w: “Where the body is, there will the vultures also be gathered together.”
k: Wheresoever the body is, thither will the eagles be gathered together.

w: and will not rather tell him, ‘Prepare my supper, clothe yourself properly, and serve me, while I eat and drink. Afterward you shall eat and drink’?
k: And will not rather say unto him, Make ready wherewith I may sup, and gird thyself, and serve me, till I have eaten and drunken; and afterward thou shalt eat and drink?

w: In that day, he who will be on the housetop, and his goods in the house, let him not go down to take them away. Let him who is in the field likewise not turn back.
k: In that day, he which shall be upon the housetop, and his stuff in the house, let him not come down to take it away: and he that is in the field, let him likewise not return back.

w: Likewise, even as it was in the days of Lot: they ate, they drank, they bought, they sold, they planted, they built;
k: Likewise also as it was in the days of Lot; they did eat, they drank, they bought, they sold, they planted, they builded;

w: “It is impossible that no occasions of stumbling should come, but woe to him through whom they come!
k: It is impossible but that offences will come: but woe unto him, through whom they come!

w: but he who didn’t know, and did things worthy of stripes, will be beaten with few stripes. To whomever much is given, of him will much be required; and to whom much was entrusted, of him more will be asked.
k: But he that knew not, and did commit things worthy of stripes, shall be beaten with few stripes. For unto whomsoever much is given, of him shall be much required: and to whom men have committed much, of him they will ask the more.

w: He said to the multitudes also, “When you see a cloud rising from the west, immediately you say, ‘A shower is coming,’ and so it happens.
k: And he said also to the people, When ye see a cloud rise out of the west, straightway ye say, There cometh a shower; and so it is.

w: They will be divided, father against son, and son against father; mother against daughter, and daughter against her mother; mother-in-law against her daughter-in-law, and daughter-in-law against her mother-in-law.”
k: The father shall be divided against the son, and the son against the father; the mother against the daughter, and the daughter against the mother; the mother in law against her daughter in law, and the daughter in law against her mother in law.

w: Do you think that I have come to give peace in the earth? I tell you, no, but rather division.
k: Suppose ye that I am come to give peace on earth? I tell you, Nay; but rather division:

w: “I came to throw fire on the earth. I wish it were already kindled.
k: I am come to send fire on the earth; and what will I if it be already kindled?

w: Don’t be afraid, little flock, for it is your Father’s good pleasure to give you the Kingdom.
k: Fear not, little flock; for it is your Father’s good pleasure to give you the kingdom.

w: He said, ‘This is what I will do. I will pull down my barns, and build bigger ones, and there I will store all my grain and my goods.
k: And he said, This will I do: I will pull down my barns, and build greater; and there will I bestow all my fruits and my goods.

w: “The ground of a certain rich man produced abundantly.
k: The ground of a certain rich man brought forth plentifully:

w: But there is nothing covered up, that will not be revealed, nor hidden, that will not be known.
k: For there is nothing covered, that shall not be revealed; neither hid, that shall not be known.

w: But if that servant says in his heart, ‘My lord delays his coming,’ and begins to beat the menservants and the maidservants, and to eat and drink, and to be drunken,
k: But and if that servant say in his heart, My lord delayeth his coming; and shall begin to beat the menservants and maidens, and to eat and drink, and to be drunken;

w: Consider the lilies, how they grow. They don’t toil, neither do they spin; yet I tell you, even Solomon in all his glory was not arrayed like one of these.
k: Consider the lilies how they grow: they toil not, they spin not; and yet I say unto you, that Solomon in all his glory was not arrayed like one of these.

k: For I will give you a mouth and wisdom, which all your adversaries shall not be able to gainsay nor resist.

w: For it will come like a snare on all those who dwell on the surface of all the earth.
k: For as a snare shall it come on all them that dwell on the face of the whole earth.

w: “Truly I tell you, this poor widow put in more than all of them,
k: Of a truth I say unto you, that this poor widow hath cast in more than they all:

w: There will be signs in the sun, moon, and stars; and on the earth anxiety of nations, in perplexity for the roaring of the sea and the waves;
k: And there shall be signs in the sun, and in the moon, and in the stars; and upon the earth distress of nations, with perplexity; the sea and the waves roaring;

w: When they are already budding, you see it and know by your own selves that the summer is already near.
k: When they now shoot forth, ye see and know of your own selves that summer is now nigh at hand.

w: Therefore be watchful all the time, praying that you may be counted worthy to escape all these things that will happen, and to stand before the Son of Man.”
k: Watch ye therefore, and pray always, that ye may be accounted worthy to escape all these things that shall come to pass, and to stand before the Son of man.

w: “Nation will rise against nation, and kingdom against kingdom.
k: Nation shall rise against nation, and kingdom against kingdom:

w: But before all these things, they will lay their hands on you and will persecute you, delivering you up to synagogues and prisons, bringing you before kings and governors for my name’s sake.
k: But before all these, they shall lay their hands on you, and persecute you, delivering you up to the synagogues, and into prisons, being brought before kings and rulers for my name’s sake.

w: “Watch out that you don’t get led astray, for many will come in my name, saying, ‘I am he
,’ and, ‘The time is at hand.’ Therefore don’t follow them.
k: Take heed that ye be not deceived: for many shall come in my name, saying, I am Christ; and the time draweth near: go ye not therefore after them.

w: Settle it therefore in your hearts not to meditate beforehand how to answer,
k: Settle it therefore in your hearts, not to meditate before what ye shall answer:

w: “See the fig tree, and all the trees.
k: Behold the fig tree, and all the trees;

w: When you hear of wars and disturbances, don’t be terrified, for these things must happen first, but the end won’t come immediately.”
k: But when ye shall hear of wars and commotions, be not terrified: for these things must first come to pass; but the end is not by and by.

w: “So be careful, or your hearts will be loaded down with carousing, drunkenness, and cares of this life, and that day will come on you suddenly.
k: And take heed to yourselves, lest at any time your hearts be overcharged with surfeiting, and drunkenness, and cares of this life, and so that day come upon you unawares.

w: There will be great earthquakes, famines, and plagues in various places. There will be terrors and great signs from heaven.
k: And great earthquakes shall be in divers places, and famines, and pestilences; and fearful sights and great signs shall there be from heaven.

w: Heaven and earth will pass away, but my words will by no means pass away.
k: Heaven and earth shall pass away: but my words shall not pass away.

w: Woe to those who are pregnant and to those who nurse infants in those days! For there will be great distress in the land, and wrath to this people.
k: But woe unto them that are with child, and to them that give suck, in those days! for there shall be great distress in the land, and wrath upon this people.

w: And not a hair of your head will perish.
k: But there shall not an hair of your head perish.

w: It will turn out as a testimony for you.
k: And it shall turn to you for a testimony.

w: You will be hated by all men for my name’s sake.
k: And ye shall be hated of all men for my name’s sake.

w: for all these put in gifts for God from their abundance, but she, out of her poverty, put in all that she had to live on.”
k: For all these have of their abundance cast in unto the offerings of God: but she of her penury hath cast in all the living that she had.

w: But when these things begin to happen, look up, and lift up your heads, because your redemption is near.”
k: And when these things begin to come to pass, then look up, and lift up your heads; for your redemption draweth nigh.

w: “But when you see Jerusalem surrounded by armies, then know that its desolation is at hand.
k: And when ye shall see Jerusalem compassed with armies, then know that the desolation thereof is nigh.

w: men fainting for fear, and for expectation of the things which are coming on the world: for the powers of the heavens will be shaken.
k: Men’s hearts failing them for fear, and for looking after those things which are coming on the earth: for the powers of heaven shall be shaken.

w: Most certainly I tell you, this generation will not pass away until all things are accomplished.
k: Verily I say unto you, This generation shall not pass away, till all be fulfilled.

w: Then let those who are in Judea flee to the mountains. Let those who are in the middle of her depart. Let those who are in the country not enter therein.
k: Then let them which are in Judaea flee to the mountains; and let them which are in the midst of it depart out; and let not them that are in the countries enter thereinto.

w: You will be handed over even by parents, brothers, relatives, and friends. They will cause some of you to be put to death.
k: And ye shall be betrayed both by parents, and brethren, and kinsfolks, and friends; and some of you shall they cause to be put to death.

w: They will fall by the edge of the sword, and will be led captive into all the nations. Jerusalem will be trampled down by the Gentiles, until the times of the Gentiles are fulfilled.
k: And they shall fall by the edge of the sword, and shall be led away captive into all nations: and Jerusalem shall be trodden down of the Gentiles, until the times of the Gentiles be fulfilled.

w: “As for these things which you see, the days will come, in which there will not be left here one stone on another that will not be thrown down.”
k: As for these things which ye behold, the days will come, in the which there shall not be left one stone upon another, that shall not be thrown down.

w: for I feared you, because you are an exacting man. You take up that which you didn’t lay down, and reap that which you didn’t sow.’
k: For I feared thee, because thou art an austere man: thou takest up that thou layedst not down, and reapest that thou didst not sow.

w: “They said to him, ‘Lord, he has ten minas!’
k: (And they said unto him, Lord, he hath ten pounds.)

w: “Go your way into the village on the other side, in which, as you enter, you will find a colt tied, which no man had ever sat upon. Untie it, and bring it.
k: Go ye into the village over against you; in the which at your entering ye shall find a colt tied, whereon yet never man sat: loose him, and bring him hither.

w: ‘For I tell you that to everyone who has, will more be given; but from him who doesn’t have, even that which he has will be taken away from him.
k: For I say unto you, That unto every one which hath shall be given; and from him that hath not, even that he hath shall be taken away from him.

w: For the Son of Man came to seek and to save that which was lost.”
k: For the Son of man is come to seek and to save that which was lost.

w: “He said to him, ‘Well done, you good servant! Because you were found faithful with very little, you shall have authority over ten cities.’
k: And he said unto him, Well, thou good servant: because thou hast been faithful in a very little, have thou authority over ten cities.

w: “He said to him, ‘Out of your own mouth will I judge you, you wicked servant! You knew that I am an exacting man, taking up that which I didn’t lay down, and reaping that which I didn’t sow.
k: And he saith unto him, Out of thine own mouth will I judge thee, thou wicked servant. Thou knewest that I was an austere man, taking up that I laid not down, and reaping that I did not sow:

w: Another came, saying, ‘Lord, behold, your mina, which I kept laid away in a handkerchief,
k: And another came, saying, Lord, behold, here is thy pound, which I have kept laid up in a napkin:

w: He called ten servants of his, and gave them ten mina coins,
and told them, ‘Conduct business until I come.’
k: And he called his ten servants, and delivered them ten pounds, and said unto them, Occupy till I come.

w: If anyone asks you, ‘Why are you untying it?’ say to him: ‘The Lord needs it.’”
k: And if any man ask you, Why do ye loose him? thus shall ye say unto him, Because the Lord hath need of him.

w: “The second came, saying, ‘Your mina, Lord, has made five minas.’
k: And the second came, saying, Lord, thy pound hath gained five pounds.

w: “It is written, ‘My house is a house of prayer,’
but you have made it a ‘den of robbers’!”
k: It is written, My house is the house of prayer: but ye have made it a den of thieves.

w: But his citizens hated him, and sent an envoy after him, saying, ‘We don’t want this man to reign over us.’
k: But his citizens hated him, and sent a message after him, saying, We will not have this man to reign over us.

w: But bring those enemies of mine who didn’t want me to reign over them here, and kill them before me.’”
k: But those mine enemies, which would not that I should reign over them, bring hither, and slay them before me.

w: and will dash you and your children within you to the ground. They will not leave in you one stone on another, because you didn’t know the time of your visitation.”
k: And shall lay thee even with the ground, and thy children within thee; and they shall not leave in thee one stone upon another; because thou knewest not the time of thy visitation.

w: He said to those who stood by, ‘Take the mina away from him, and give it to him who has the ten minas.’
k: And he said unto them that stood by, Take from him the pound, and give it to him that hath ten pounds.

w: “If you, even you, had known today the things which belong to your peace! But now, they are hidden from your eyes.
k: If thou hadst known, even thou, at least in this thy day, the things which belong unto thy peace! but now they are hid from thine eyes.

w: For the days will come on you, when your enemies will throw up a barricade against you, surround you, hem you in on every side,
k: For the days shall come upon thee, that thine enemies shall cast a trench about thee, and compass thee round, and keep thee in on every side,

w: “I tell you that if these were silent, the stones would cry out.”
k: I tell you that, if these should hold their peace, the stones would immediately cry out.

w: “Zacchaeus, hurry and come down, for today I must stay at your house.”
k: Zacchaeus, make haste, and come down; for to day I must abide at thy house.

w: Then why didn’t you deposit my money in the bank, and at my coming, I might have earned interest on it?’
k: Wherefore then gavest not thou my money into the bank, that at my coming I might have required mine own with usury?

w: “So he said to him, ‘And you are to be over five cities.’
k: And he said likewise to him, Be thou also over five cities.

w: “A certain nobleman went into a far country to receive for himself a kingdom, and to return.
k: A certain nobleman went into a far country to receive for himself a kingdom, and to return.

w: The first came before him, saying, ‘Lord, your mina has made ten more minas.’
k: Then came the first, saying, Lord, thy pound hath gained ten pounds.

w: “Today, salvation has come to this house, because he also is a son of Abraham.
k: This day is salvation come to this house, forsomuch as he also is a son of Abraham.

w: “When he had come back again, having received the kingdom, he commanded these servants, to whom he had given the money, to be called to him, that he might know what they had gained by conducting business.
k: And it came to pass, that when he was returned, having received the kingdom, then he commanded these servants to be called unto him, to whom he had given the money, that he might know how much every man had gained by trading.

w: Then they will begin to tell the mountains, ‘Fall on us!’ and tell the hills, ‘Cover us.’
k: Then shall they begin to say to the mountains, Fall on us; and to the hills, Cover us.

w: “Assuredly I tell you, today you will be with me in Paradise.”
k: Verily I say unto thee, To day shalt thou be with me in paradise.

w: “Daughters of Jerusalem, don’t weep for me, but weep for yourselves and for your children.
k: Daughters of Jerusalem, weep not for me, but weep for yourselves, and for your children.

w: For if they do these things in the green tree, what will be done in the dry?”
k: For if they do these things in a green tree, what shall be done in the dry?

w: “So you say.”
k: Thou sayest it.

w: For behold, the days are coming in which they will say, ‘Blessed are the barren, the wombs that never bore, and the breasts that never nursed.’
k: For, behold, the days are coming, in the which they shall say, Blessed are the barren, and the wombs that never bare, and the paps which never gave suck.

w: “Father, forgive them, for they don’t know what they are doing.”
k: Father, forgive them; for they know not what they do.

w: “Father, into your hands I commit my spirit!”
k: Father, into thy hands I commend my spirit:

w: “Why were you looking for me? Didn’t you know that I must be in my Father’s house?”
k: How is it that ye sought me? wist ye not that I must be about my Father’s business?
